clue.text: In public admitting the subject of unnecessary analysis

indicators.note: the word for admitting is placed in the word for public, so In signals the insertion

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
though can mean admitting that, conceding a point

explanation.surface: Someone, speaking openly, concedes that a matter has been analysed to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In public' looks like a single phrase; split it so 'In' is the container instruction. Though in the sense 'admitting that' is a concession.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overthought has been pondered far more than it needed, so it is what excessive analysis was applied to.

clue.text: Completely at fault, loudly dismissed

definitions.meaning: fourth meaning: a batter is ... in cricket

explanation.walkthrough: Four separate senses; 'dismissed' is the cricket one, where a batter's innings ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists all four senses: thoroughly, in error, audibly, and no longer batting in cricket.

clue.text: Tests to pass cryptic solver's afternoons?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: examinations one must get through
second meaning: read as ..., former mornings, which a crossword mind takes as afternoons

explanation.walkthrough: A.M. is morning; something that is ex-morning has become afternoon, the kind of reading only a cryptic solver makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Exams are formal assessments that students must succeed in, here punningly split as past mornings.

clue.text: Its members have managed to get it up

definitions.text: Its members have managed to get it up

parts.words: Its members have managed to get it up
parts.note: the risqué reading is of those who have had sex aboard an aeroplane in flight

explanation.walkthrough: A society's members seem to have hoisted something; 'up' means up in the air, and the double entendre is deliberate.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is a jocular term for people who have had sex on board an aircraft in flight.

clue.text: Bound over till cleared of wrongful charges cooking up big deal

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: cooking up means concocting, so these letters are mixed into a new order
a till cleared of something has it taken out, so those letters go

parts.note: taken as written
ill means wrong or harmful, as in ill-gotten

explanation.surface: Someone is bound over until acquitted, while scheming a major business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: TILL loses ILL to leave T; 'cooking up' rearranges O, T and BIG DEAL together.
explanation.definitionFit: Obligated means bound by duty or law to do something, under compulsion.

clue.text: Right? Wrong size

indicators.note: wrong means incorrect, so the letters of right are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone checks a clothing size and finds it doesn't fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right?' and 'Wrong' set up a contradiction; one is the fodder, the other the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Girth is the measurement around something's middle, its bulk or circumference.

clue.text: Lose sleep, not the newly-designed camera gear!

indicators.note: something newly designed has been reworked, so the letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Advice not to fret overnight about the new photographic equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Telephoto lenses are long-focus camera optics that magnify distant subjects.

clue.text: Scotty's expressed impatience round Kirk?

parts.note: a round thing is a ring, the letter O
kirk is the Scottish word for church, abbreviated CH

explanation.surface: Star Trek's engineer Scotty sighs impatiently at Captain Kirk.
explanation.walkthrough: Kirk looks like the Star Trek captain, but here it is the Scottish church; Scotty here is any Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: Och is a Scottish exclamation voicing irritation or impatience, the sort a Scot might utter.

clue.text: A tricky fix to be let out when one's dropped in it?

definitions.text: A tricky fix to be let out when one's dropped in it?

indicators.note: dropped in means put inside, so the numeral goes into the rearranged letters
tricky implies twisting things about, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is one is

explanation.surface: A hopeless predicament from which no one is released once thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges BE LET OUT, and 'dropped in' puts I (one) inside it. 'A', 'fix to' and 'when' belong to the definition and joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: An oubliette is a dungeon reached only by a trapdoor above, where prisoners were dropped and forgotten.

clue.text: Tug (probably tender) may get one where reservoirs are following suit

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this part goes after the suit

parts.note: hearts is a suit of playing cards
Tring, a Hertfordshire town, is known for the Tring Reservoirs

explanation.surface: A tender tug boat follows to where the reservoirs lie.
explanation.walkthrough: Tring is a small town in Hertfordshire, England, famous for its nature-reserve reservoirs. Tender here means lovingly, not a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A heartstring is a deep emotion; a tender appeal is said to tug at someone's heartstrings.

clue.text: Someone perhaps working at Bettys who can bring up a cloth?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ..., as at Bettys, the famous Yorkshire tea rooms

definitions.text: who can bring up a cloth
definitions.meaning: second meaning: one who teasels, raising the nap on cloth with teasel heads

explanation.walkthrough: Bettys is a celebrated chain of tea rooms in Harrogate and York. Split the answer as TEA SELLER for the first sense; read whole, it is someone who teasels fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea seller serves tea in a café; a teaseller raises the nap of woven fabric using teasel burrs.

clue.text: Participant in bar billiards tipped the scales

indicators.note: tipped means tipped over, so the letters found are read in the opposite direction
a participant is part of something, so the letters sit inside the words bar billiards

explanation.surface: A pub game player weighed in heavily, tipping the scales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Participant in' finds ARBIL across bar billiards; 'tipped' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra is the zodiac sign and constellation represented by a pair of balances.

clue.text: Not being sharpest knife in drawer will doubtless be this

definitions.text: Not being sharpest knife in drawer will doubtless be this

parts.words: Not being sharpest knife in drawer will doubtless be this
parts.note: a dim person fails to grasp an argument, and a blunt knife literally lacks its tip

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not the sharpest knife in the drawer' is an idiom for being dim; a blunt knife is also literally without its tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Failing to understand the central argument is the figurative sense; a knife lacking its tip is the literal one.

clue.text: Middle English promise to keep unusually shtum?

definitions.text: Middle English promise to keep unusually shtum?

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so these letters sit within
unusually signals the letters of shtum appear in an unusual order

parts.note: your word is a promise

explanation.surface: An old English vow to stay remarkably quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Shtum is Yiddish-derived slang for silent, which is exactly what the answer urges, so the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an injunction to keep a secret, a pledge to stay silent.

clue.text: Hosts cut trick shot

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: hosts as in great numbers, masses

explanation.surface: Party hosts snip a film's flashy stunt shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hosts' looks like people giving a party; it means multitudes.
explanation.definitionFit: A massé is a billiards or pool stroke with a steeply raised cue that makes the ball swerve.

clue.text: "Sun fruit" — cool flavouring

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sun, as in Sunday or the sun
a pear is a fruit
mint is slang for excellent, cool

explanation.surface: A tropical fruit produces a refreshing taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a herb whose oil is used to give taste to gum, toothpaste and sweets.

clue.text: Despot's last Italian stronghold close to retribution

indicators.note: the last of a despot's letters is the one taken

parts.note: final letter of despot
It is the short form of Italian, as in It vermouth
a fort is a stronghold
at means near, close to

explanation.surface: A tyrant's final Italian fortress lies near the place of vengeance.
explanation.definitionFit: Tit for tat means repaying an injury in kind, a matching retaliation.

clue.text: Into the bargain is carrying lustreless and harmful fruit

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so these letters go inside

parts.note: too means also, in addition, into the bargain
matt or mat means without shine, lustreless
ill means harmful, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A deal includes dull, poisonous produce.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomatillo is a small husked fruit from Mexico, related to the tomato, used in salsa verde.

clue.text: First sign of authority now missing from head made it sparkly

definitions.text: First sign of authority now missing from head made it sparkly

indicators.note: sparkly suggests a glittering new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the opening letter of authority is the one removed

parts.note: first letter of authority, A, is what goes missing

explanation.surface: Without its symbol of power, a royal head was adorned with something glittering.
explanation.walkthrough: Take HEAD MADE IT, remove A, the first letter of authority ('now missing from'), and 'sparkly' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Diadem, the George IV State Diadem, is a jewelled crown worn on the head and a sign of royal authority.

clue.text: Signs double claim to be discharged at intervals

indicators.note: letters are let go one after another, so only every other one survives

explanation.surface: Indicators say a two-fold insurance claim will be paid in instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are printed marks such as the dagger or division symbol, used to flag doubtful passages.

clue.text: Explosion in Tehran this great?

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so these words are blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A huge blast in the Iranian capital, of tremendous size.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth-shattering means enormous in impact, as of a blast so large it seems to shake the globe.

clue.text: Within reach are many wives!

indicators.note: within means inside, so the letters sit inside the words reach are many

explanation.surface: Plenty of spouses are close at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' does double duty in setter's spirit but is needed for both the hidden letters and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the women of a polygamous household, a group of wives or concubines.

clue.text: Island's "swinging", guide is wanting to put about?

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter goes
swinging is slang for bisexual, BI

indicators.note: put about means turned round, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: an A to Z is a street-map guide, AZ

explanation.surface: A holiday island is called a swinging place by a guide who wants to spread the word.
explanation.walkthrough: No parse is fully settled; the clue is loose. AZ is an A–Z street atlas, a staple of British cities. The charade still reads I + BI + ZA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is one of Spain's Balearic islands, famed for its nightlife.

clue.text: Oxford college recess

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a bay window projecting from an upper storey

explanation.definitionFit: Oriel is one of the Oxford colleges, and an oriel window forms a projecting bay or alcove.

clue.text: Pleased with pub-free second edition?

indicators.note: free of something means without it, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a second edition is a republishing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted with a reissue that has no bar scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pub-free' looks like a hyphenated adjective; split it so 'pub' gives the letters and 'free' removes them.
explanation.definitionFit: Relishing something means enjoying it greatly, taking delight in it.

clue.text: Fathers of Savoy Opera inhaling a substance

indicators.note: inhaling means taking in, so this letter goes inside

parts.note: Gilbert and Sullivan, G and S, created the Savoy operas

clue.text: Serve short time period

parts.note: to do can mean to serve, as in do for or do a sentence
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Serving a brief stint in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serve short time' reads as a prisoner's sentence; 'period' is the full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a period is the punctuation mark; a dot is the same small mark.

clue.text: People in the house cadge food from boy

parts.note: to bum is to cadge or scrounge
from boy read as boy's, SON'S
eats is slang for food

explanation.definitionFit: Bums on seats is an idiom for paying audience members filling a theatre.
